Pick among (a) order-preserving encode, (b) targeted string substitution, (c) correct the claim instead -- or determine the sizing call itself needs CODE-DESIGNER.

result.summary:
BLOCKING PROCESS FINDING FIRST: the code this issue is about does not exist on this branch. fix/ISS-0442-lint-handoffs-autofix-diff-20260903 was cut from main (via the ISS-0444 merge, commit ee3f858c). --autofix/write_json!/2 were added by commit a33b5b1d 'feat(ISS-0440): --dir and restricted --autofix on letflow.lint_handoffs', which lives ONLY on origin/feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903 -- confirmed NOT an ancestor of HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor a33b5b1d HEAD` fails) and NOT merged to main (`git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903 main` fails; docs/issues/ISS-0440.yaml itself still reads `status: open`, no PR exists for that branch per `gh pr list`). lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex on this branch (768 lines, verified by full read) has no `autofix`/`write_json` token at all -- grep confirms zero hits. CODE-DESIGNER cannot design this fix against this branch's checked-out tree; it must design against origin/feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903's version of the file (or ORCH must first land ISS-0440 to main and rebase this branch on top). I proceeded with diagnosis by reading and reproducing against origin/feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903 directly (via a disposable git worktree, since no elixir/mix toolchain is available in this sandbox per README's documented constraint) so the diagnosis itself is not blocked, but implementation cannot start until this dependency is resolved -- flagging for ORCH.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed against origin/feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903, file lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex): `autofix_file/1` (~line 414) does `data |> Map.put("status", to) |> write_json!(path)` on the FULL decoded map for a legal-value fix; `write_json!/2` (~line 454-457) is `encoded = Jason.encode!(data, pretty: true); File.write!(path, encoded <> "\n")`. Two compounding effects, not just the one the issue names: (1) `Jason.decode/1` returns a plain map with no key-order metadata, so `Jason.encode!/2` re-sorts every level's keys alphabetically (top-level AND every nested object -- context, task, result, git_evidence, etc. all get resorted, not just the top level as the issue's prose implies); (2) independently of ordering, `pretty: true` re-flows every value's formatting (short arrays that were inline, e.g. `["a", "b"]`, get exploded to one-element-per-line; a file originally minified to one line gets fully re-wrapped). Effect (2) means even a file whose keys happened to already be alphabetical would still get a large diff if it wasn't already in Jason's own pretty-print style. The existing comment at ~450-453 only reasons about effect (1) (key order) and about machine consumers (H3 checks membership not order) -- it does not address effect (2), and does not address human/agent reviewers at all, which is the actual gap ISS-0442 names.

REPRODUCTION (real, quoted numbers): mix/elixir is not installed in this sandbox (confirmed: `which elixir mix` empty; README documents this constraint independently for `mix deps.get`), so I could not invoke the mix task directly. I instead extracted the real function pair's exact semantics from the source and reproduced them with an equivalent Python simulation (json.load -> mutate one key -> json.dump(..., indent=2, sort_keys=True), which is exactly what Jason.encode!(data, pretty: true) does: 2-space indent, alphabetical keys, no attempt at stable ordering) against a REAL handoff file already checked out on that branch: handoffs/WF03-ISS0392-20260901/step-00-git-setup.json (48 lines, pretty-printed, a genuine handoff, not a synthetic fixture). Simulated: set top-level status from COMPLETED to DONE (an --autofix-map key), then ran the equivalent of `write_json!` to fix DONE -> COMPLETED. Measured with `diff -u orig.json autofixed.json`: 88 diff lines on a 48-line file -- i.e. essentially the ENTIRE file changed (every top-level key line, several nested object key lines, and multiple array/string reflow lines), consistent with and slightly worse than the issue's own 84-line figure (different fixture, same order of magnitude, same root cause). This independently confirms the issue's reproduction rather than just re-quoting it, and additionally confirms effect (2) above is real: several of the 88 changed lines are pure reflow (e.g. `"owned_modules": ["lib/letflow/engine.ex", "lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex"]` on one line in the original becomes a 4-line array), not key reordering at all.

OPTION (a) FEASIBILITY -- jason version: mix.lock pins `jason 1.4.5`; mix.exs declares `{:jason, "~> 1.4"}`. `Jason.OrderedObject` (order-preserving decode/encode round trip) is a real jason feature but was NOT present in 1.4.x -- it shipped later in the 1.x line. Because mix.exs's constraint is `~> 1.4` (permits any 1.x, not pinned to 1.4.x specifically), a version bump would not need a mix.exs edit, only a `mix.lock` update (`mix deps.update jason`), which needs hex.pm network access -- unavailable in this sandbox per README's already-documented `mix deps.get` constraint, so ELIXIR-DEV would need to do that step on a networked host, same as any other deps.get-requiring change. This is a dependency-version bump, not a wholly new dependency, so decision 0014's new-dependency policy is not squarely triggered, but it is not a zero-risk, zero-decision change either: `Jason.OrderedObject` decodes into a distinct struct, not a plain map, so H1-H4's existing pattern matches (`check_h1_status(path, %{"status" => status})`, etc., all written against plain maps) would need to change shape too, or the ordered decode would need to be used ONLY on the --autofix write path (decode twice: once as a plain map for linting, once as an OrderedObject only inside write_json!/2, re-encoding only the OrderedObject). That branching is itself a design decision with more than one reasonable shape.

OPTION (b) RISK -- confirmed real, not hypothetical: the reproduction fixture itself (handoffs/WF03-ISS0392-20260901/step-00-git-setup.json) has BOTH a top-level `"status"` key (legal-status domain: PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED) AND a nested `result.status` key (result-value domain: PASS/FAIL) -- and `@autofix_map`'s domain includes `"PASS" => "COMPLETED"`, so a handoff with top-level status `PASS` (an actual documented defect class -- ISS-0440 itself was filed over exactly this: ELIXIR-DEV writing top-level status PASS) sitting alongside a nested `result.status: "PASS"` (which is CORRECT and must not change) is a real, not contrived, collision case for any 'find the status line and substitute' approach. A naive first-match-in-file-order substitution happens to work only because top-level keys are serialized before the nested `result` object in every sample file examined -- that is an incidental property of current serialization order, not a guaranteed invariant a targeted-substitution implementation could safely rely on without either verifying it structurally (which starts to require a JSON-aware scan, not a plain string substitution) or adding a test that would catch the ordering assumption breaking. This matches exactly the caveat the issue's own text already flagged for option (b) ('needs care with escaping and with a status value appearing elsewhere in the file') -- confirmed with a real fixture, not a guess.

SIZING VERDICT: route to CODE-DESIGNER, not a mechanical ISSUE-FIXER/ELIXIR-DEV fix. Reasoning: (1) the correct option is not obviously (b)-with-no-real-risk -- the PASS/PASS collision case above is real and demonstrated on an actual file, not speculative; (2) option (a) is feasible but carries its own non-trivial design fork (decode-twice-with-different-shapes vs. refactor all four hard-check functions to handle OrderedObject) that a wrong default choice would ripple through H1-H4; (3) this directly affects a security-relevant reviewability property SECURITY-REVIEWER already relied on for ISS-0440's sign-off, so per this session's own standing guidance a wrong pick here is exactly the kind of mistake that should get independent design review rather than an ISSUE-FIXER shortcut; (4) option (c) (correct the claim instead of the code) is only legitimate if (a)/(b) prove disproportionate, which is itself a judgment call CODE-DESIGNER, not ISSUE-FIXER, should make and justify. No fix was implemented by this agent, per WF-03's diagnose/design separation.

ADDITIONAL FLAG FOR ORCH (not part of the CODE-DESIGNER routing, but load-bearing for sequencing): this fix cannot be implemented, security-reviewed, or tested on a branch that lacks the --autofix code at all. Either (i) land origin/feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903 to main first and rebase fix/ISS-0442-lint-handoffs-autofix-diff-20260903 on top before dispatching CODE-DESIGNER's implementation step, or (ii) have CODE-DESIGNER/ELIXIR-DEV target origin/feature/WF03-ISS0440-20260903 directly and let the two land together. This diagnosis handoff and its routing target are valid either way since the diagnosis was performed against the feature branch's real code, but the next step's git setup needs to account for this before ELIXIR-DEV can touch a file that, on the current branch, doesn't yet exist.
